mu-e4aeb253.stem: Which is the main muscle that extends the elbow?
mu-e4aeb253.explanation: Triceps brachii is the three-headed muscle on the back of the arm; it inserts on the olecranon and extends the elbow, assisted by anconeus.

mu-b6e8a730.stem: In general, what movement do the muscles of the anterior (flexor) compartment of the forearm produce?
options: They flex the wrist and fingers
They extend the wrist and fingers
mu-b6e8a730.explanation: The anterior forearm compartment contains the wrist and finger flexors and the pronators; most arise from the medial epicondyle and are supplied by the median nerve. The posterior compartment contains the extensors.

mu-6af834e1.stem: What is the muscular bulge at the base of the thumb called?
mu-6af834e1.explanation: The thenar eminence is formed by abductor pollicis brevis, flexor pollicis brevis and opponens pollicis; the bulge at the base of the little finger is the hypothenar eminence.

mu-ecb2c9e2.stem: Which nerve supplies most of the small (intrinsic) muscles of the hand?
mu-ecb2c9e2.explanation: The ulnar nerve supplies the hypothenar muscles, interossei, 3rd–4th lumbricals, adductor pollicis and the deep head of FPB. The median nerve supplies the thenar muscles and the 1st–2nd lumbricals.

mu-0e70d6e5.stem: Which is the largest and most superficial muscle of the gluteal region?
mu-0e70d6e5.explanation: Gluteus maximus is the most superficial and largest muscle of the buttock; it is the strongest extensor of the hip and is used in rising from sitting and climbing stairs.

mu-cfe6d009.stem: Which is the strongest flexor of the hip?
mu-cfe6d009.explanation: Iliopsoas (psoas major and iliacus) inserts on the lesser trochanter and is the strongest flexor of the hip.

mu-c868aa3f.stem: Which hip abductor keeps the pelvis level when standing on one leg during walking?
mu-c868aa3f.explanation: Gluteus medius (and minimus) abducts the hip on the stance side and prevents the opposite side of the pelvis from dropping. Its paralysis produces a positive Trendelenburg sign.

mu-43cd6d79.stem: Which four-headed muscle on the front of the thigh extends the knee?
mu-43cd6d79.explanation: Quadriceps femoris consists of rectus femoris and the three vasti; its common tendon encloses the patella and, via the patellar ligament, inserts on the tibial tuberosity to extend the knee.

mu-91b50ba3.stem: What movement do the hamstring muscles on the back of the thigh produce at the knee?
mu-91b50ba3.explanation: The hamstrings (biceps femoris, semitendinosus, semimembranosus) extend the hip and flex the knee.

mu-9430014d.stem: What is the common function of the muscles of the medial compartment of the thigh?
options: Moving the thigh away from the midline (abduction)
Bringing the thigh towards the midline (adduction)
mu-9430014d.explanation: The medial compartment muscles – adductor longus, brevis, magnus, gracilis and pectineus – adduct the thigh; most are supplied by the obturator nerve.

mu-f30b91ef.stem: Which muscle group forms the calf and inserts on the heel via the Achilles tendon?
mu-f30b91ef.explanation: The two heads of gastrocnemius and soleus insert on the calcaneal tuberosity through the common Achilles tendon; they are the strongest plantar flexors of the ankle (rising on tiptoe).

mu-4b00481c.stem: Which muscles are found in the lateral compartment of the leg?
options: Tibialis posterior and flexor digitorum longus
Tibialis anterior and extensor hallucis longus
mu-4b00481c.explanation: The lateral compartment contains fibularis longus and brevis; they evert the foot and are supplied by the superficial fibular nerve.

mu-26fd811e.stem: What type of muscle tissue are skeletal muscles made of?
mu-26fd811e.explanation: Skeletal muscles are cross-striated and voluntary, not involuntary; they are supplied by somatic motor nerves. Smooth muscle is found in the walls of internal organs, cardiac muscle in the heart.

mu-f3107df4.stem: Which is the smallest skeletal muscle of the body?
mu-f3107df4.explanation: Stapedius is a muscle of about 1 mm in the middle ear attached to the stapes; it damps stapes movement in loud sound, protecting the inner ear, and is supplied by the facial nerve.

mu-87a9939b.stem: What is the bony attachment of a muscle that stays fixed during movement called?
mu-87a9939b.explanation: The origin is usually the proximal, fixed attachment; the insertion is the attachment on the bone that moves. When a muscle contracts, the insertion approaches the origin.

options: From the temporal fossa and temporal fascia
mu-68e69843.explanation: Temporalis arises from the floor of the temporal fossa and the fascia covering it; it passes deep to the zygomatic arch to insert on the coronoid process.

mu-a88fccee.stem: What is the main function of buccinator?
options: Pressing the cheek against the teeth to keep food between them during chewing, and blowing
Raising the corner of the mouth
mu-a88fccee.explanation: Buccinator is the muscular layer of the cheek; it stops food escaping between cheek and teeth and tightens the cheek when blowing (playing the trumpet). It is supplied by the facial nerve and pierced by the parotid duct.

mu-20439cf3.stem: Which muscle pulls the corner of the mouth down (sad expression)?
mu-20439cf3.explanation: Depressor anguli oris runs from the lower border of the mandible to the corner of the mouth and pulls it down. Zygomaticus major pulls the corner upwards and outwards (smiling).

mu-c19c6bea.stem: Which muscle divides the neck into anterior and posterior triangles?
mu-c19c6bea.explanation: The anterior triangle lies in front of SCM, the posterior triangle between SCM and trapezius. Omohyoid and digastric subdivide these triangles into smaller ones.

options: From the posterior tubercles of the C1–C4 transverse processes
From the anterior tubercles of the C3–C6 transverse processes
mu-ca04a98c.explanation: Scalenus anterior arises from the anterior tubercles of the C3–C6 transverse processes and inserts on the scalene tubercle of the 1st rib; the phrenic nerve descends on its front.
